newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - June 10.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

WASHINGTON - Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston withdrew his name from consideration for chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, deciding that to fight for the job would risk too bruising a confirmation battle.

WASHINGTON - In the current climate, shaped by the aborted court-martial of Air Force Lt. Kelly Flinn and the sex scandal at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Gen. Joseph Ralston could not win Senate confirmation as the nation's top military commander.

WASHINGTON - Eight database companies, including the well-known Lexis Nexis online search service, have agreed to limit the kinds of information they assemble about ordinary people and to more closely monitor who uses that data.

WASHINGTON - President Bill Clinton vetoed a bill to provide disaster relief money to help flood-stricken states, leaving Republicans scrambling for a plan to counter his charge that they were "playing politics with the lives of Americans in need".

WASHINGTON - Congressional Republicans offered their first detailed plan for lowering taxes as part of this year's balanced budget deal, unveiling a five-year, $85 billion tax cut package that would benefit many parents, students, investors and corporations.

WASHINGTON - Ruthann Aron, a Potomac developer who ran for the Maryland Senate nomination in 1994, was arrested yesterday on charges that she tried to hire a man to kill her husband and a Baltimore lawyer, police said.
